bibl.title: The future of digital health with federated learning

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: federated learning as an answer to data governance and privacy constraints in healthcare machine learning
span.quote: Federated learning (FL)9–11 is a learning paradigm seeking to address the problem of data governance and privacy by training algorithms collaboratively without exchanging the data itself.

span.label: how to train on medical data that cannot be centralised
span.quote: By enabling multiple parties to train collaboratively without the need to exchange or centralise data sets, FL neatly addresses issues related to egress of sensitive medical data.

span.label: a consensus perspective on what FL offers digital health and what it still requires
span.quote: However, FL still requires rigorous technical consideration to ensure that the algorithm is proceeding optimally without compromising safety or patient privacy.

span.label: prediction
span.quote: Not all technical questions have been answered yet and FL will certainly be an active research area throughout the next decade

span.label: medical data sitting in silos that machine learning cannot reach
span.quote: Another reason why data sharing is not systematic in healthcare is that collecting, curating, and maintaining a high-quality data set takes considerable time, effort, and expense. Consequently such data sets may have significant business value, making it less likely that they will be freely shared.

span.label: a perspective paper: no new experiment, performance claims cited from prior work
span.term: a perspective paper: no new experiment, performance claims cited from prior work
span.quote: Recent research has shown that models trained by FL can achieve performance levels comparable to ones trained on centrally hosted data sets and superior to models that only see isolated single-institutional data16,17.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: MOVE THE MODEL, NOT THE DATA: training happens locally inside each institution and only model characteristics leave the firewall, so the consensus model is built without the patient records ever being pooled
span.quote: FL enables gaining insights collaboratively, e.g., in the form of a consensus model, without moving patient data beyond the firewalls of the institutions in which they reside. Instead, the ML process occurs locally at each participating institution and only model characteristics (e.g., parameters, gradients) are transferred as depicted in Fig. 1.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: WHY ANONYMISATION CANNOT BE THE ANSWER: identity survives the removal of the obvious fields - a face is reconstructable from a CT scan, and a handful of record elements permits reidentification
span.quote: Even if data anonymisation could bypass these limitations, it is now well understood that removing metadata such as patient name or date of birth is often not enough to preserve privacy7.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: DATA IS WITHHELD FOR COMMERCIAL REASONS AS WELL AS LEGAL ONES: curating a high-quality set costs time and money, which gives it business value and makes sharing less likely - a motive no privacy technology addresses
span.quote: Another reason why data sharing is not systematic in healthcare is that collecting, curating, and maintaining a high-quality data set takes considerable time, effort, and expense. Consequently such data sets may have significant business value, making it less likely that they will be freely shared.

span.label: FL is stated to still require rigorous technical consideration to avoid compromising safety or patient privacy - the paradigm is offered as promising rather than solved
span.quote: However, FL still requires rigorous technical consideration to ensure that the algorithm is proceeding optimally without compromising safety or patient privacy.

span.label: The authors say plainly that not all technical questions have been answered and expect FL to remain an open research area for a decade
span.quote: Not all technical questions have been answered yet and FL will certainly be an active research area throughout the next decade

span.label: The performance claim is attributed to other work rather than demonstrated here - this is a perspective paper citing comparisons, not running them
span.quote: Recent research has shown that models trained by FL can achieve performance levels comparable to ones trained on centrally hosted data sets and superior to models that only see isolated single-institutional data16,17.

span.label: Public medical data carries varying license restrictions that sometimes limit its exploitation, which bounds what any centralised alternative could have used anyway
span.quote: Public medical data is usually task- or disease-specific and often released with varying degrees of license restrictions, sometimes limiting its exploitation.

span.label: Federated learning
span.quote: Federated learning (FL)9–11 is a learning paradigm seeking to address the problem of data governance and privacy by training algorithms collaboratively without exchanging the data itself.

span.label: data governance
span.quote: Federated learning (FL)9–11 is a learning paradigm seeking to address the problem of data governance and privacy by training algorithms collaboratively without exchanging the data itself.

span.label: consensus model
span.quote: FL enables gaining insights collaboratively, e.g., in the form of a consensus model, without moving patient data beyond the firewalls of the institutions in which they reside. Instead, the ML process occurs locally at each participating institution and only model characteristics (e.g., parameters, gradients) are transferred as depicted in Fig. 1.

span.label: anonymisation
span.quote: Even if data anonymisation could bypass these limitations, it is now well understood that removing metadata such as patient name or date of birth is often not enough to preserve privacy7.

span.label: reidentification
span.quote: Anonymised data from the electronic health record can appear innocuous and GDPR/PHI compliant, but just a few data elements may allow for patient reidentification7. The same applies to genomic data and medical images making them as unique as a fingerprint38.

span.label: privacy
span.quote: Federated learning (FL)9–11 is a learning paradigm seeking to address the problem of data governance and privacy by training algorithms collaboratively without exchanging the data itself.

span.label: precision medicine
span.quote: By enabling multiple parties to train collaboratively without the need to exchange or centralise data sets, FL neatly addresses issues related to egress of sensitive medical data.

span.label: license restrictions
span.quote: Public medical data is usually task- or disease-specific and often released with varying degrees of license restrictions, sometimes limiting its exploitation.

span.label: egress
span.quote: By enabling multiple parties to train collaboratively without the need to exchange or centralise data sets, FL neatly addresses issues related to egress of sensitive medical data.

span.label: business value
span.quote: Another reason why data sharing is not systematic in healthcare is that collecting, curating, and maintaining a high-quality data set takes considerable time, effort, and expense. Consequently such data sets may have significant business value, making it less likely that they will be freely shared.

span.label: firewalls
span.quote: FL enables gaining insights collaboratively, e.g., in the form of a consensus model, without moving patient data beyond the firewalls of the institutions in which they reside. Instead, the ML process occurs locally at each participating institution and only model characteristics (e.g., parameters, gradients) are transferred as depicted in Fig. 1.

span.label: anonymisation - TREATED HERE AS INSUFFICIENT BY CONSTRUCTION, not as imperfect in practice: removing name and date of birth does not preserve privacy, a face can be reconstructed from a CT scan, and genomic data is as unique as a fingerprint
span.quote: Even if data anonymisation could bypass these limitations, it is now well understood that removing metadata such as patient name or date of birth is often not enough to preserve privacy7.
